questions.stem: Which assemblage is the minimum MQSA definition of a mammography unit?

choices.text: Generator, control, tube housing, beam-limiting device, and supporting structures
choices.rationale: Correct. These are the minimum components in § 900.2(dd).

choices.text: Only a digital detector and a compression paddle
choices.rationale: A detector and paddle alone omit required components.

choices.text: Any general radiographic room plus a mammography attachment
choices.rationale: General-purpose systems with attachments are prohibited.

choices.text: A mobile coach without an x-ray control
choices.rationale: An x-ray control is required.

questions.explanation: MQSA defines a mammography unit as including at least generator, control, tube housing assembly, beam-limiting device, and supports.

variants.simpler: Five parts minimum: make x-rays, control them, house the tube, limit the beam, and support them.
variants.example: If a schematic omits the beam-limiting device, it is incomplete.

questions.stem: A clinic proposes using a general radiographic unit fitted with a mammography compression attachment. Under MQSA, this is:

choices.text: Allowed if a medical physicist surveys it annually
choices.rationale: Surveys do not legalize prohibited equipment.

choices.text: Allowed for screening but not diagnostic exams
choices.rationale: The prohibition is not limited by exam type.

choices.text: Prohibited; mammography must use equipment specifically designed for mammography
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Allowed only with DBT software enabled
choices.rationale: Software does not override the equipment prohibition.

questions.explanation: General-purpose or specially attached non-mammography systems shall not be used for mammography.

variants.simpler: No bolting a paddle onto a general room.
variants.example: Accreditation will not save a prohibited configuration.

questions.stem: Along the primary beam path, which component sits between the tube housing and the compression paddle?

choices.text: Image receptor
choices.rationale: The receptor is beyond the breast.

choices.text: Beam-limiting device
choices.rationale: Correct. It shapes the field before the paddle and breast.

choices.text: Acquisition workstation
choices.rationale: Displays are not in the beam path.

choices.text: PACS archive
choices.rationale: Storage is not in the beam path.

questions.explanation: Order: tube housing → beam-limiting device → paddle → breast → support/receptor.

variants.simpler: Shape the beam before it hits the patient.
variants.example: Collimation problems point to the beam-limiting device.

questions.stem: Which component produces the x-rays in a mammography unit?

choices.text: Beam-limiting device
choices.rationale: It shapes the field.

choices.text: Compression paddle
choices.rationale: It compresses tissue.

choices.text: Tube housing assembly
choices.rationale: Correct. X-rays are produced in the tube within the housing.

choices.text: Image receptor
choices.rationale: It detects remnant radiation.

questions.explanation: The tube housing assembly contains the x-ray tube where electrons strike the anode.

variants.simpler: X-rays start in the tube housing.
variants.example: No exposure? Think generator/control/tube first.

questions.stem: Bremsstrahlung x-rays are produced when:

choices.text: An outer-shell electron falls without a vacancy being created
choices.rationale: Characteristic emission needs a vacancy.

choices.text: Electrons decelerate in the anode
choices.rationale: Correct. Bremsstrahlung means braking radiation.

choices.text: Photons scatter from the paddle toward the receptor
choices.rationale: That is not anode production.

choices.text: The grid absorbs scatter after the breast
choices.rationale: Grid action is after production.

questions.explanation: OpenStax: deceleration of electrons in the anode produces bremsstrahlung.

variants.simpler: Braking radiation = electrons slowing in the anode.
variants.example: The continuous spectrum under characteristic peaks is bremsstrahlung.

choices.text: The electron binding energies of the anode material
choices.rationale: Correct. Energies identify the anode element.

choices.text: The matrix size of the digital detector
choices.rationale: Detector sampling is unrelated.

choices.text: Whether the grid is in or out
choices.rationale: Grid status does not set characteristic energies.

questions.explanation: Characteristic x-rays are emitted when inner-shell vacancies are filled; energies are characteristic of the anode element.

variants.simpler: If you cannot see it on the image as an attribute, it is not on the list.
variants.example: Exposure level (too light/dark) is different from a dose measurement.

questions.stem: Between accreditation clinical image reviews, certified facilities must:

choices.text: Ignore image quality until the next 3-year submission
choices.rationale: Ongoing compliance is required.

choices.text: Continue producing clinical images that meet their accreditation body's quality standards
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Stop using compression to save time
choices.rationale: Compression remains necessary.

choices.text: Disable labeling to reduce artifacts
choices.rationale: Labeling is required and is itself an attribute.

questions.explanation: § 900.12(i): clinical images must continue to comply with the AB's clinical image quality standards.

variants.simpler: Quality is everyday, not only every 3 years.
variants.example: EQUIP asks how you check yourselves between reviews.

questions.stem: A technically well-positioned image shows a deodorant speck projected over axillary tissue. Which attribute is most clearly failed?

choices.text: Examination identification
choices.rationale: Labeling is not the issue described.

choices.text: Artifacts
choices.rationale: Correct. External material obscures/mimics structures.

choices.text: Outcomes audit PPV
choices.rationale: Audit metrics are unrelated to this single image defect.

choices.text: Modality definition
choices.rationale: Modality definition is not an image attribute.

questions.explanation: Artifacts include external material that obscures or mimics anatomy.

variants.example: Prevent with clear pre-exam instructions.

questions.stem: ALARA means:

choices.text: As large as regulators allow
choices.rationale: Opposite idea.

choices.text: As low as reasonably achievable
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Average lung and rib assessment
choices.rationale: Not a radiation term.

choices.text: Automatic lateral and right angulation
choices.rationale: Not a radiation term.

questions.explanation: CDC: ALARA = as low as reasonably achievable.

variants.simpler: Keep dose low when you can.
variants.example: Even small non-beneficial doses should be avoided.

questions.stem: CDC's three basic ALARA protective measures are:

choices.text: Time, distance, and shielding
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: kVp, mAs, and grid
choices.rationale: Technique factors, not the ALARA triad.

choices.text: PPV, sensitivity, and specificity
choices.rationale: Performance metrics.

choices.text: Certification, accreditation, and inspection
choices.rationale: MQSA program features.

questions.explanation: Time, distance, and shielding are the three basic measures.

variants.simpler: Less time, more distance, use a barrier.
variants.example: Technologists stepping behind a barrier is the clinic example.

questions.stem: The NRC's linear no-threshold (LNT) model assumes that:

choices.text: Below 100 mSv, radiation is proven to be risk-free
choices.rationale: NRC notes data do not absolutely establish risk there, yet still uses LNT conservatively.

choices.text: Any increase in dose, no matter how small, results in an incremental increase in risk
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Only alpha particles can cause cancer
choices.rationale: Many radiation types are implicated at high doses.

choices.text: Mammography beams are non-ionizing
choices.rationale: X-rays are ionizing.

questions.explanation: NRC accepts LNT as a conservative model: incremental dose → incremental risk estimate.

variants.simpler: LNT = no safe threshold assumed for protection math.
variants.example: Use it to support careful technique, not to terrify patients.

history.note: Touches dose, thresholds, or device-specific practice; keep out of verified pools until qualified review.

questions.stem: NCI describes mammography as an imaging test that uses:

choices.text: High-dose therapeutic radiotherapy beams
choices.rationale: Mammography is diagnostic imaging, described as low-dose.

choices.text: Low-dose x-rays
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Only magnetic fields
choices.rationale: That describes MRI.

choices.text: Ultrasound exclusively
choices.rationale: Mammography uses x-rays.

questions.explanation: NCI: mammography uses low-dose x-rays to create pictures of the breast.

variants.example: Still practice ALARA.

questions.stem: OpenStax locates the key molecular target for ionizing-radiation effects in cells at:

choices.text: Keratin in nails only
choices.rationale: Not the key target discussed.

choices.text: DNA molecules
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Dietary calcium in calcifications
choices.rationale: Calcifications are imaging findings, not the cellular target.

choices.text: Lead in aprons
choices.rationale: Shielding material, not a cellular target.

questions.explanation: Ionizing radiation affects molecules within cells, particularly DNA; it can interfere with reproduction and function.

variants.simpler: DNA is the critical target in this teaching.
variants.example: That is why rapidly dividing cells are especially sensitive.
